description: Celestica DS6000 - 3U, 64-port 1.6TbE OSFP224 data centre switch on a Broadcom Tomahawk 6 (102.4 Tbps) with an Intel Xeon-D COM Express CPU and a RunBMC/OpenBMC service processor. The front is a black perforated bezel carrying sixteen columns of OSFP224 cages, each column two stacked pairs numbered top to bottom, with a management and timing cluster across the top right: two RJ45 consoles (CON0, CON1), two 50GbE SFP56 management ports, an RJ45 GbE MGMT port, an RJ45 ToD port, 1PPS and 10 MHz SMA jacks, a USB 3.0 Type-A, a USB-C console, a reset pinhole and four system lamps. The rear carries five fan modules (4+1, dual-rotor) across the top and four 3200 W supplies (2+2) across the bottom between two legend panels, the left one with the grounding point. No installation guide exists for this model; it is drawn from the datasheet and from vendor renders.

Which way each OSFP block faces. The render shows a riding heat sink inside every block, so both ports of a block face the same way, and the lower block's latch marks sit at its bottom where the upper block's sit at its top - 0/0 over 180/180 - but no orthographic elevation of this face is held. An installation-guide elevation or a square-on photograph settles it; until then every pair is held in stack-exceptions.

name: ds6000

airflow-colour.note: STORDIS names the rear render "Rear_Front_To_Back", and its fan bars, fan latches, supply bails and supply latches are all red; ds6000-A-3 agrees. This is the F2B AC build (R4087-F9004-A1). The B2F build's handle colour is unseen and is not assumed; see gaps.

chassis.note: Height 129.8 mm, width 438 mm, depth 712.2 mm, 35 kg, 3U - datasheet PHYSICAL DIMENSIONS. 438 is the body between the rack-ear folds: the square-on renders show the ears (front: pale handle brackets with green thumbscrews; rear: grey brackets) standing outside a body whose own width is what scales to 438. Ears and handles are not drawn. COLOUR follows the ruling for every Celestica switch - a black faceplate on an otherwise silver chassis: chassis.color is the sheet metal (#c4c8cc, which the rear, lid and sides show on every render) and the front's black is a full-face `bezel` decor (#16181b).

gate-1.note: MARGINAL ON THE FRONT, FAILS ON THE REAR, SO EACH AXIS IS SCALED BY ITS OWN DATASHEET DIMENSION. The front bezel reads 938 x 275 px (x 131.5-1069.5, y 260.5-535.5 by threshold on the black plate), aspect 3.411 against 438/129.8 = 3.374, 1.1% out. The rear body reads 916 x 266.5 px (x 140.5-1056.5, y 83.8-350.3), aspect 3.437, 1.9% out. Both renders run SHORT in height by the same sense, which says the difference is in the renders or in what the datasheet height includes (feet, a lid lip) rather than in either edge reading, and neither image has a feature of independently known size to settle it. So x is taken as a fraction of 438 and y as a fraction of 129.8, and every position is quoted to +/-0.5 mm, the size of one render pixel. The front's column pitch was then checked for perspective: fifteen cage-frame left edges fit a straight line at 26.616 mm with residuals under 0.25 mm and no trend, so the render is orthographic across the row.

lifecycle.note: Launched 2025-10 (datasheet rev 100725, press release 2025-10-10). The Foleon product page is live and carries the datasheet; no end-of-sale or end-of-life notice was found on it, on the STORDIS page or in the intake's searches, so none-announced.

lug-tag.note: A pull-out luggage tag at the bottom right, "LUG TAG" printed above it at (393.5, 123.4) and the model name on the tab itself, 381.8-405.2 across at the bottom edge on ds6000-F. celestica/lug-tag@1 (23.0 x 4.0) is placed centred on it, LANDSCAPE (rotate 0) because this tag lies along the bottom edge rather than standing on end as on the DS3000/DS4000. The label is "DS6000", legible on ds6000-A and as a blur on ds6000-F. Which end carries the pull lip does not resolve on either render; the part's own lip-right is kept.

power.note: "2+2 redundant, hot swappable AC/DC 3200W PSUs", "180-240VAC auto-ranging, 47-63Hz /40-72VDC input". The datasheet gives NO chassis power figure - no typical, no maximum - so power-max-w is not written, and no per-fan figure either. "Up to 32W / 40W transceivers" is recorded as the optics budget.

sources.note: A DATASHEET AND VENDOR RENDERS, AND NO INSTALL GUIDE. Celestica DS6000 datasheet rev 100725 (2 pp, Foleon, byte-identical to the STORDIS mirror) is the only document; the intake confirmed that Celestica's documentation portal stops at the DS5000 and every DS6000 install-guide URL pattern returns 404. Six images are staged: the square-on front (ds6000-F, 1200 x 800, and ds6000-F-2, the same render with a STORDIS callout) and square-on rear (ds6000-B, 1200 x 661, labelled front-to-back, with STORDIS callout discs over the supplies and the middle fan) from the STORDIS product page, and three Foleon three-quarter renders (ds6000-A 3626 px, ds6000-A-2, ds6000-A-3 front and rear stacked). Positions come from the square-on pair; the three-quarter renders were used for identity, legends and counts only (counting-is-not-measuring). No vendor 3D model was found on either product page.

the-esd-jack-and-wordmark.note: "Celestica" is printed at the top left of the bezel, x 3.4-26.6, cap band 5.9-9.8, and set here as plain text, which the no-logos rule permits for a wordmark. The ESD jack below it is visible only on ds6000-A (the square-on render is black there); its "ESD" legend reads at (8.7, 20.0) on ds6000-F and the jack is placed centred above the legend by proportion from ds6000-A, so its y is estimated to about a millimetre.

the-management-cluster.note: Bright-object bounding boxes on ds6000-F, x 205-430 mm, y 3-26 mm: CON0 211.1-227.4 and CON1 234.4-251.2 (white RJ45 housings), SFP56 M1 259.2-274.1 and M2 281.1-296.0 (bezel 12.3-24.5 down) with a green lamp and "SFP56" above each and "M1", "M2" below, MGMT 304.0-320.8 (dark jack with lamps in its upper corners), TOD 327.8-344.1 (white), 1PPS and 10MHz SMA nuts 7.0 mm across at 355.1 and 367.7 (silver, drawn as panel decor round std/sma@1 because common/sma-jack@1's nut is gold), the USB-A and USB-C shells drawn as panel decor round their std/ openings. ALL FOUR RJ45s ARE KEYWAY UP: on ds6000-A at 3.6k px every jack's opening is narrow at the top (the latch slot) and wide at the bottom where the contacts show, and MGMT's lamps sit in the keyway-side corners, so all four are std/rj45@2 / common/rj45-eth@1 at rotate 180. Continuing: the USB-A shell standing vertical at 381.5 with its SuperSpeed "SS" mark beside it, the USB-C console vertical at 394.6, RST at 406.4 and the four lamps ALM/FAN over SYS/PSU at 417.2/424.2 by 15.0/20.4. The RJ45s are placed on one centreline (15.95); the render's scatter is 0.2 mm. Identities are confirmed by the legible legends on ds6000-A. The render shows a small oval outline just left of the USB-C that no document explains; it is not drawn (see gaps).

the-osfp-wall.note: SIXTEEN COLUMNS OF TWO STACKED PAIRS, NUMBERED DOWN EACH COLUMN. Each column holds two blocks, each block a 2x1 stacked OSFP cage: a bright metal shell 24.3 mm wide and 35.0 tall with a white perforated band 7.5 mm tall between its two apertures. The three- quarter render ds6000-A shows the band and the two openings clearly at 3.6k px; on the square-on render the band reads as the lighter strip mid-block. Shell frames fit x = 7.15 + 26.616 i (i = 0..15), so column centres are 19.3 + 26.616 i, symmetric about the face centre to 0.2 mm; blocks span y 35.4-70.4 and 78.1-113.1. The OSFP apertures are std/osfp@1's 23.1 x 13.5 centred in each shell half, which the 35.0 block height carries with 0.25 mm to spare at each end. ORDER, from the legend printed between the blocks and legible on ds6000-A: `1 (bar-triangle-up) 2 (up)(down) 3 (down-triangle-bar) 4` - port 1 is the top aperture of the upper block, 2 its bottom, 3 the top of the lower block, 4 its bottom; column 2 is 5-8, and so on to 61-64. STACKS are drawn upper 0 / lower 180 per block, and that turn is HELD, NOT SETTLED (#799). The white band is a riding heat sink - the OSFP MSA rev 5.22's riding-heatsink stacked cage, which seats both ports of a block the same way up (section 7.1, Table 7-1) - and on ds6000-A-3 the lower block's two light marks sit at the bottom of its lower port where the upper block's sit at the top of its upper port, which reads as 0/0 over 180/180. No orthographic elevation of this face is held, so the turn is left as drawn, every pair is named in stack-exceptions, and the gap stacked-osfp-orientation says what settles it.

the-port-lamps.note: FOUR ROUND LENSES PER COLUMN, TWO ABOVE THE UPPER BLOCK AND TWO BELOW THE LOWER, at the column centre +/-9.8 mm and y 31.7 / 116.7. ds6000-A shows each as a round window with a bright dot, sitting at the ends of the perforated strip over each block; on ds6000-F they are the small bright marks at the ends of those strips. Four per column is one per port, but WHICH PORT EACH SERVES IS NOT PUBLISHED: with no install guide there is no LED table, and position alone cannot say whether the left lens above a block serves its top or its bottom port. Each lamp therefore names its block's two ports collectively, and the port-lamp-assignment gap records the question. led-dot@1 at 2 mm is the size read.

the-port-legends.note: One legend row per column on a baseline at 75.1 mm between the two blocks, 2.2 mm type, averaged over all sixteen columns on ds6000-F: the first port's numeral and bar-topped up-triangle span -10.3 to -6.5 mm from the column centre, the middle pair's numerals and up/down triangles -4.2 to +4.2, the last port's bar-bottomed down-triangle and numeral +6.5 to +10.7. The bars are drawn as short strokes over the first triangle and under the last. The rule runs to the last column: ds6000-A shows "61 62 63 64" in the same form.

the-rear.note: ds6000-B, x as a fraction of 438 over 916 px and y of 129.8 over 266.5 px. FIVE FAN MODULES across the top on an 85.47 mm pitch from x 7.56, each 81.8 x 83.4 from y 3.0. FOUR SUPPLIES across the bottom on a 77.49 mm pitch from x 65.9, y 88.0-129.4 frame; the crps-1u 73.5 x 40 envelope is centred in each frame. Two fixed legend panels flank the supplies, 5.5-62.6 and 375.6-432.7 across. The left panel prints the earth symbol, "fan 1 up, fan 2 right-right, fan 3 right-right-right" on its top row and "PSU 1 right, PSU 2 right-right" below; the right panel "fan 4 left-left, fan 5 up" and "PSU 3 left-left, PSU 4 left" - arrows pointing from the panel to the module each names, which is how the modules are numbered 1-5 and 1-4 left to right as seen from the rear. The fan-1 legend and the earth symbol are legible only on ds6000-A-3 (the square-on render shows that corner as a blank patch) and are placed by proportion from it. Two stud holes at (10.1, 109.2) and (10.1, 119.0) on ds6000-B take a two-hole lug, which ds6000-A-3 shows fitted. A yellow two-symbol hazard label sits under the legends on each panel.

the-vent-fields.note: The bezel is perforated with small square holes almost everywhere the ports and jacks are not; ds6000-A resolves them as roughly 2 mm squares on about 2.6 mm. Three fields are drawn - above the OSFP wall left of the management cluster, and the strip under it, split round the LUG TAG - each on a backing rect (vent-field-needs-backing-rect). Their extents are the areas the square-on render shows as textured, not measured hole by hole.

stack-exceptions.reason: HELD AS DRAWN, NOT A READING OF THIS TURN (#799). The product render ds6000-A-3.png shows a riding heat sink, the white finned band, between the two ports of every 2x1 block - the OSFP MSA rev 5.22's riding-heatsink stacked cage, which seats both ports the same way up (section 7.1, Table 7-1) - so neither block is the 0/180 drawn here. And the lower block's openings carry their two light marks at the BOTTOM of the lower port where the upper block's sit at the TOP of the upper port, so the lower block looks like the upper turned over: 0/0 over 180/180, as on the DS5000's elevation. No elevation of this face is held to confirm it, so the geometry is held until it is decided; the gap stacked-osfp-orientation says what settles it.
